title: Close what is already done or obsolete
why: These look done in a comment, superseded, or moot. Skim the list, Skip any you want to keep, then close the rest with the button below; each gets a one-line comment saying why.

title: npm: add a trusted publisher to each package
why: One form per package, identical except for the repo and workflow file. Do them back to back.
steps: Open the package's settings link below and sign in with your passkey once.
Under Trusted publishing, choose GitHub Actions. Fill owner, repository and workflow file name (the card says which). Leave environment empty unless the card names one.
Save. Then under Publishing access choose 'Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens' and save.
A new configuration expires unless a publish uses it soon, so tell the session which packages you did; it can trigger their publish workflows.

title: npm: first publish of new packages
why: A package must exist on npm before a trusted publisher can be attached, so its first version needs your login. A session does the work; your phone only approves.
steps: Send the card's prompt (or one prompt naming all of them) to a session.
The session runs npm login --auth-type=web, then npm publish --auth-type=web for each package. Each prints a link: open it on the phone and approve with your passkey.
Then add the trusted publisher for each new package (the run above).

title: npm: claim scopes and orgs
why: Each is a short web form.
steps: Open the link, create or claim the org, add yourself as owner.

title: PyPI: add trusted publishers
why: One form per project. Existing projects use the project's Publishing settings; new ones use a pending publisher on your account page.
steps: Add a GitHub publisher: owner, repository, workflow file name, environment if the card names one.

title: PyPI: releases waiting on you
why: Mostly a go-ahead plus a session run.

title: Create API keys and accounts
why: Each needs you in a browser for a minute; a session then stores the key and runs the check. Never paste a key into GitHub or this board; paste it only into the session.
steps: Open the console link and create the key.
Copy the card's prompt into a session on the machine it names, then paste the key when the session asks.

title: One-off live checks with a real key
why: A session runs these. Many only need a key already on the machine.

title: GitHub settings
why: Repo settings are not in GitHub Mobile: use the phone browser and request the desktop site if a page is cramped.

title: Server chores for a session
why: Paste each prompt into a session on the machine it names. They can go in one message.

title: Dependency bump PRs
why: Green ones only. Major bumps can break the app; skim the PR's checks first.

title: PRs waiting on your review
why: GitHub Mobile: Files changed, then Review changes, then Approve, then merge.

title: Record yourself
why: Batch these into one sitting with headphones.

title: Listen or look and judge
why: Batch these into one sitting with headphones.

title: Mac day
why: Out of bounds from the phone. Every card keeps its links and prompt so nothing needs rediscovering.
